notes: Global electricity demand rose by 849 TWh, or 2.8%, in line with the ten-year average of 2.7%. Clean power, meaning renewables plus nuclear, rose by 887 TWh, more than the rise in demand. Fossil generation fell by 38 TWh, the first year without a rise since 2020. Inside fossil, coal fell 63 TWh, gas rose 36 TWh and oil and other fossil fell 12 TWh. The IEA points the same way: renewables plus nuclear grew by more than total generation.
